grammar.topic: Present perfect vs simple past: when to use which in work updates
grammar.explanation:
Use the SIMPLE PAST (worked, fixed, deployed) when the action happened at a finished, specific time, either stated or clearly understood: yesterday, last sprint, on Monday, in 2023, two hours ago, when I was at Google. Use the PRESENT PERFECT (have/has + past participle: have fixed, has deployed) when the time is unspecified or still open (today, this week, this sprint, so far, already, yet, just, ever, since, for), or when the result matters now.

Key rules:
1) A finished time word means simple past. Never combine the present perfect with 'yesterday', 'last week', 'ago', 'in March', or 'when...'.
2) An open period or a focus on the current result means present perfect. 'This week I've closed five tickets' works because the week isn't over.
3) In stand-ups, open with the present perfect for the headline, then switch to the simple past for the details: 'I've finished the migration. I ran it on staging yesterday and it took 20 minutes.'
4) For experience in interviews, use the present perfect for life experience with no time given ('I've worked with Kafka') and the simple past once you name the job or time ('At Flipkart I built a Kafka consumer...').

Examples:
- I've fixed the login bug, so you can test it now. (result matters now)
- I fixed the login bug yesterday afternoon. (finished time)
- We've had three incidents this month. (month still open)
- We had three incidents last month. (finished period)
- Have you ever used Terraform? Yes, I used it at my last company to manage AWS infra.

commonErrors.wrong: I have deployed the fix yesterday.
commonErrors.why: 'Yesterday' is a finished time, so it needs the simple past.
'Since' plus something that is still true needs the present perfect, not the present simple.

commonErrors.wrong: Did you finish the PR yet?
commonErrors.right: Have you finished the PR yet?
commonErrors.why: 'Yet' signals an open time frame, so standard (especially British) English uses the present perfect. The simple past with 'yet' is acceptable in casual American speech, but the present perfect sounds more professional.

commonErrors.wrong: I have joined the company two years ago.
commonErrors.right: I joined the company two years ago.
commonErrors.why: 'Ago' always marks a finished point in time, so it needs the simple past.

commonErrors.wrong: In my last job I have led a team of five.
commonErrors.right: In my last job I led a team of five.
commonErrors.why: The last job is a finished period, so it takes the simple past.

exercises.prompt: I ___ (merge) the PR about ten minutes ago.
exercises.explanation: 'Ago' marks a finished time, so it needs the simple past.

exercises.prompt: So far this sprint, we ___ (close) 14 tickets.
exercises.explanation: 'So far' and 'this sprint' describe an open period, so they need the present perfect.
'Ever' asks about life experience with no specific time, so it needs the present perfect.

exercises.prompt: We have released version 2.3 last Friday.
exercises.explanation: 'Last Friday' is a finished time, so the sentence needs the simple past.

exercises.prompt: I am on the payments team for three years.
exercises.answer: I have been on the payments team for three years.
exercises.explanation: The action started in the past and continues now ('for three years'), so it needs the present perfect.

exercises.prompt: I've just finished the refactor. I've started it on Monday and I've hit a tricky race condition on Tuesday.
exercises.answer: I've just finished the refactor. I started it on Monday and hit a tricky race condition on Tuesday.
exercises.explanation: The headline uses the present perfect because the result matters now. The details with specific days ('on Monday', 'on Tuesday') switch to the simple past.

speaking.prompt: Give your daily stand-up update for yesterday and today. Cover what you've finished, what you did yesterday in detail, any blockers, and your plan for today.
tips: Open with a present perfect headline ('I've finished X'), then switch to the simple past for the details ('I tested it on staging yesterday').
Keep it under 90 seconds and end with a clear blocker or 'no blockers'.
usefulPhrases: I haven't been able to ... yet because...

speaking.prompt: You are leading a short incident review. Explain what happened during a production outage last week, what the team has done since then, and what is still pending.
tips: Use the simple past for the incident timeline ('At 3 p.m. the API started timing out').
Use the present perfect for follow-up actions ('We've added an alert, and we haven't migrated the DB yet').
usefulPhrases: Since then, we've put in place...

speaking.prompt: Answer the question: 'Tell me about yourself and your experience.' Talk about your overall experience, then one specific past role or project.
tips: Summarize your career with the present perfect ('I've been a backend engineer for five years').
Switch to the simple past when you name a company or project ('At X, I built...').
usefulPhrases: I've been working in ... for about ... years.
One project I'm proud of is when I...

speaking.prompt: Explain a technical topic simply: describe what caching is and why it makes apps faster, as if the interviewer were a non-technical product manager. Then mention one time you used caching in a project.
tips: Use an everyday analogy (keeping frequently used items on your desk instead of in the storage room) before any jargon.
Use the present simple for the explanation and the simple past for your real example.
usefulPhrases: In one project, we used it to cut response time from ... to ...

speaking.prompt: A colleague at the coffee machine asks, 'How's your week been?' Chat for one to two minutes about your week so far and something you did last weekend.
tips: 'This week' is still open, so use the present perfect ('It's been busy, I've had lots of meetings').
For the weekend, use the simple past ('I went hiking on Saturday').
usefulPhrases: It's been a pretty ... week so far.

speaking.prompt: Tell a friend about a new tool, app, or gadget you've started using recently: how long you've had it, what you've liked so far, and one moment when it really helped you.
tips: Use 'for' and 'since' with the present perfect ('I've used it for two weeks').
Tell the 'helpful moment' as a short story in the simple past.
usefulPhrases: The other day it actually saved me when...

writing.prompt: Write a Slack message (4-6 sentences) to your manager giving a weekly status update: what you've completed this week, what you did on a specific day, and what you haven't done yet.
writing.tip: Start with present perfect results ('I've shipped...'), use the simple past only with specific days, and finish with 'haven't ... yet' for pending work.

writing.prompt: Write a short LinkedIn 'About' paragraph (5-6 sentences) describing your overall experience and one past achievement at a named company.
writing.tip: Use the present perfect for your career summary ('I've built...') and the simple past for the achievement at the named company ('At X, I reduced...').
